instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Thirty-seven starts and an England call-up; fit for a whole season for the first time, and comfortably his best.
Seven starts at 32 after a season in Malaysia.
Thirteen goals at 34; a limited but genuinely effective penalty-box striker to the end.
His best season: a good passer for a centre-half of that era, and Liverpool's first choice.
Fitness and weight problems cost him the place, and a good deal of the ability with it.
A regular in a Sunderland side relegated with 19 points, the lowest total in the division’s history at the time; evidence about the side more than the player.
Six seasons on from his last rated year, most of them in the Championship; a thirty-three-start regular for a promoted Wolves at 34, with five goals from set pieces.
Thirty-six and at Sunderland, still a competent starter.
Sixteen league goals at twenty for a promoted side; excellent hold-up and a genuine finisher, held short of 80 because the work rate and movement were not.
Fifteen goals in twenty-six starts for an Everton side that finished fifth; the best season of his career.
A ruptured Achilles in November ended the season; rated on the forward he was before it.
Back from the Achilles rupture heavier and a yard slower, and never the same forward again.
Eight goals from midfield for Sunderland after a record fee; his most productive season.
Still Liverpool’s best player, but slower since the 1991 Achilles rupture.
Reinvented as a central midfielder after the Achilles injury and very good at it; the pace was gone, the football was not.
Two starts at 34 for Charlton.
Age 33 and half a season of minutes; the passing range was still there but the legs were going.
Thirty-seven and still starting; the range of pass outlasted the mobility by several years.
The season he became England first choice at right back and made the PFA side; the attacking quality well ahead of the defending.
An ever-present and West Ham's captain, which is evidence about the side; a small, honest defender with no top-flight attribute that travels to a modern squad.
Thirty-three, two starts, and well below the standard of the division by then.
The best version of him: direct, quick, and a genuine problem for full-backs in a title-challenging side.
Seven starts for a relegated Leicester; a fringe player by 28.
Twenty-seven starts for a relegated Sheffield United at 31, three years on from his last top-flight season; the pace that was his whole game had gone.
Nine assists and the best football of his career for a promoted side, two years on from the last rated season.
Five years and two divisions on from Sheffield Wednesday; a first-choice centre-half for a promoted Portsmouth at 28 and a better organised defender than he was at 23.
Seventeen starts for a Bradford side relegated with twenty-six points; second-tier standard.
Footballer of the Year in half a season. Elite rather than 90+: a wonderful technician in a side that finished sixth, not a best-in-the-world claim.
Thirty-three and rotated; four league goals, still the best passer at the club.
Nineteen starts at 35 and used more sparingly than ever.
Fourteen league goals at 36 and Chelsea’s player of the season — a genuine late revival rather than sentiment.
Every outfield position and an emergency spell in goal for a promoted side; a good defender doing a utility job.
An England call-up before the cruciate injury; the season the centre-back was fully formed.
On loan from Metz at 19 and plainly athletic and sharp; rated as the prospect, not the Fulham and Manchester United striker.
Three years on from five appearances at Newcastle as a 19-year-old.
A seven-point rise: thirteen goals in twenty Fulham starts, then seven in nine after the January move to Manchester United. Same number at both clubs - one player, one season.
A seven-point rise: thirteen goals in twenty Fulham starts, then seven in nine after the January move to Manchester United. Same number at both clubs - one player, one season.
Seven starts; a knee injury rather than a loss of ability.
His most complete United season for availability; sharp, quick and a genuine handful when fit.
Thirteen goals in twenty-six Everton starts at thirty; the ability held up better than the fitness.
Sold to Aston Villa in September 1992 after six starts for Liverpool.
Three league goals in 33 starts for a relegated Forest; the finishing had gone well before the legs.
Veteran squad forward at 35, useful for movement and link play rather than goals.
Four starts at 36 in his final season; no longer a top-flight footballer.
A January arrival who took half a season to adjust; rated as the player of those months, not the one he became.
A European Cup and the PFA side; among the best left backs in the world by now.
Thirty-four and a Juventus regular; still an excellent full back, plainly past the United peak.
England international and the quickest centre-half in the division; injuries took him apart afterwards.
Thirty-six starts and six goals after years of injury at Newcastle — fit for a whole season for the first time since 1995/96.
Thirteen starts for a relegated Leicester at 31; the pace that made him was gone.
Twenty, and already one of the quickest and most technically able midfielders in the division.
Fifteen starts - the hamstring trouble that shaped his career; rated on the player when fit, which was unchanged.
Thirty-three starts in a Newcastle side that finished third, and England’s first-choice right-sided midfielder; his most complete season.
Four starts; injury again, and rated on the player when fit as the seasons either side of it are.
The double leg break in 2007 finished him. Three years and four starts later he was no longer a top-flight footballer.
Eight starts in two years at West Ham; the pace and the body both gone.
Eighteen goals at twenty-one; a finisher of genuine top-flight quality with very little else in the game.
Twenty-four goals for a mid-table side and an England place; the best version of a narrow player.
Seventeen league goals across a January move; the same footballer at both clubs.
Seventeen league goals across a January move; the same footballer at both clubs.
An attacking wing-back of genuine international quality — a Romania regular across two World Cups — in a role English football barely used.
Thirty-two and split between Bradford and Southampton; the legs had gone but the delivery and positioning had not. The same player at both clubs.
Thirty-two and split between Bradford and Southampton; the legs had gone but the delivery and positioning had not. The same player at both clubs.
Moved to West Ham in the Julian Dicks exchange, September 1993.
Three clubs in one season - West Ham, Everton and then Coventry - and the same player at all three.
Three clubs in one season - West Ham, Everton and then Coventry - and the same player at all three.
Three clubs in one season - West Ham, Everton and then Coventry - and the same player at all three.
Thirty-three and still the best footballer in the Keegan side.
Thirty-five, and Shearer's arrival plus a fading engine reduced him to a rotation option.
Thirty-six and at Bolton; effectively finished.
Signed as a squad addition and used across the back line and in midfield; not yet a Premier League centre-half.
Converted into Leeds’ first-choice centre-half under George Graham. A real step up in role and in standard, not drift.
Captain of a side that finished third and reached a European semi-final; quick, brave and an outstanding recovery defender. Very good rather than elite.
Nineteen starts; knee trouble began to interrupt him.
Two years of knee surgery on, at 33, and a shadow of the recovery defender he had been.
Eleven starts in a relegation season, effectively a ceremonial captain by then.
Five starts at 33; a squad forward well below top-flight standard.
Twelve goals in eighteen starts for a relegated side, with far better feet and link play than the caricature allows. Still not an elite forward.
Five years on from his last rated season, at 32 and a regular for a relegated Palace side; the delivery was still decent, nothing else was.
Eleven goals from midfield for a side that finished fourth, and the most dangerous aerial midfielder in the division — a shade below the Fellaini season rated 83 for the same profile.

Half a season in each division after a January move; one player, one number.

Young Player of the Year the season before and a better footballer in this one; the beating of a full back either way.
Thirty-four and relegated; ten starts and clearly finished at this level.
An eleven-match ban for pushing the referee split the season across two clubs. Nothing changed about the player, so the rating is the same at both.

Nine goals in sixteen starts but a peripheral, disruptive figure in a relegated side.
Twelve assists at 35, and almost entirely a standing playmaker by this point.
A converted midfielder in his first season at right-back; the athleticism carried him, the positioning was learned later.
A dependable, athletic starter at right-back for the Invincibles; good rather than elite in his own right.
Cruciate ligament damage in January ended his season and, in effect, his Arsenal career.
Nine starts at Portsmouth; the knee had taken the athleticism the whole of his game was built on.
Eighteen, already quick and positionally sound enough for Wenger to use in a title season, but a long way from the France international he became.
Thirty-seven starts and the PFA team of the year at twenty-two.
